openings.claim: Freezing prepared storage positions during the evening may remove movement-linked locator upkeep while retaining prompt, correct pickup for readers and the sole clerk.
openings.delta: Keep prepared books stationary; newly arrived holds remain on the existing cart. Repair existing exception entries before opening within ten minutes. Do not claim cart capacity or speed is established.
openings.prediction: At comparable arrival volume and book size, stationary positions reduce stale-location searches with less upkeep than updating every movement.
openings.rival_prediction: Movement updates are necessary because arrivals exceed cart capacity or accessible stationary storage; freezing positions produces congestion and slower retrieval.
openings.defeat: Observed cart overflow, inaccessible holds, unchanged second searches, or preparation exceeding ten minutes defeats this branch.
openings.probe: Propose one bounded evening using existing shelves, cart, slip and timing sheet. The clerk checks storage feasibility and times all preparation before adopting stationary positions; stop before changes if the cap or capacity fails. Retain private names and recipient checks; record total pickup time and wrong handoffs.
assumptions: Cart capacity and stationary retrieval feasibility are unconfirmed.
Existing recipient verification remains required; improved outcomes are untested.

openings.claim: Can existing private reservation information distinguish the reserving reader from another household member reliably enough to prevent wrong-reader handoffs?
openings.delta: Test identity-to-hold matching feasibility before treating reliable matching as an available capability.
openings.prediction: For a small behind-desk preparation sample, the clerk can resolve household-name discrepancies uniquely using existing information.
openings.rival_prediction: Existing records identify only a household or conflicting surnames; ambiguous holds remain unresolved despite accurate locations.
openings.defeat: Any sampled mismatch lacking a unique, supportable recipient match defeats the claim that verification is already available.
openings.probe: Within the same ten-minute daily preparation budget, inspect a small sample privately without changing handoffs. Record resolved versus unresolved matches on existing paper; retain ordinary handoff verification. This tests feasibility, not zero-error performance.
assumptions: Access to adequate reservation information is unconfirmed.
The sample cannot establish population-wide reliability.

critiques.issue: Movement-linked updates depend on feasible upkeep during peak demand; stopping at a cap does not establish sustained operation. Q1 removes movement upkeep while explicitly retaining capacity uncertainty.
Reliable identification of each moved hold is assumed despite household mismatches. Q2 distinguishes adequate existing records from unresolved identity ambiguity before intervention.
